_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
The terminal does not treat a disconnected socket as a shell exit. The test seeded a conversation at /c/term-disconnect. Call "dropSocket" drops the network connection of the browser's terminal websocket for this conversation (the one opened with its conversation_id), as a lost network would; it returns "dropped", or "no socket" if there was none. "The terminal input" is the visible terminal's input, '.terminal-panel-content [data-terminal-id][style*="display: block"] textarea[aria-label="Terminal input"]' (other terminals' inputs are hidden); to type into it, focus it with an eval (.focus()), then use type steps, which type key by key, and press_key for Enter or Control+d. 
1. Navigate to /c/term-disconnect. Send "!" (fill [data-testid="message-input"] with it and click [data-testid="send-button"]). There should be exactly 1 ".terminal-panel-tab-running".
2. Call "dropSocket"; it should return "dropped".
3. There should be exactly 1 ".terminal-panel-tab-error".
4. Reload. There should be exactly 1 ".terminal-panel-tab-running" (the shell still runs).
5. Type "exit" into the terminal input and press Enter. There should be no ".terminal-panel-tab" (count 0).
